control_implications.headline: SonicWall SonicOS added to CISA KEV catalog
control_implications.significance: The addition to the KEV catalog signals active exploitation requiring immediate asset identification and remediation. Vulnerability and asset owners should confirm affected SonicWall deployments and verify patch deployment or compensating controls.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: A single attacker using AI agents pulled emergency dispatch records covering seven Taipei districts, researchers at Acronis's Threat Research Unit said last week. The agents also found a Taipei fire department platform exposing patient data from 2018, including ECG readings and ambulance video footage, without a login.
control_implications.headline: Taipei fire department platform exposes patient data
control_implications.significance: Unauthenticated exposure of sensitive health data via automated AI-driven collection indicates critical gaps in data access controls. Data and privacy owners should confirm authentication requirements for all patient data repositories and validate audit log coverage for unauthorized access detection.

paragraphs.text: CISA added a SonicWall SonicOS authentication bypass to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog while threat actors rapidly exploit an OpenSSH flaw allowing passwordless sign-in, and researchers demonstrated complete takeover of automotive mobile apps via default credentials on a ForgeRock identity platform. These developments indicate active exploitation of authentication weaknesses across network perimeter, remote access, and identity provider layers. Control owners should prioritize asset identification for SonicWall and OpenSSH deployments, verify privileged credential rotation on identity platforms, and confirm that monitoring covers exploitation attempts against these vectors.

A Web3Auth authentication flaw enabled cryptocurrency wallet theft, AI agents extracted sensitive patient data from an unauthenticated fire department platform, and a third-party cloud service breach exposed 7.7 million customer records at Iris Ohyama. These incidents highlight cascading risks from third-party dependencies and inadequate data access controls. Data protection and supplier risk owners should assess Web3Auth and cloud service provider assurances, validate that sensitive data repositories require authentication, and ensure incident response plans address third-party compromise scenarios.
